The high pure metal powder ( ≥ 99.95 wt%) of Mn, Fe, Co, and Ni with equal atomic ratio was milled for 20 h in a planetary ball mill under an argon atmosphere to produce HEA powders.
The entire sintering process was conducted under a low vacuum of 10-1 Pa and cooled with the furnace after holding at 1050 ◦ C and 50 MPa for 1h.
The sintered bulk HEAs were immersed in liquid nitrogen and cooled to its temperature before being deformed under a hydraulic press. The overall thickness was reduced by 10 %.
The deformed HEA samples were then annealed at 500 ◦ C, 600 ◦ C, 700 ◦ C, and 800 ◦ C for 30 min, followed by water quenching.

The XRD results indicate that the MnFeCoNi HEAs consist of a matrix phase (FCC) and a precipitated phase ( σ phase).
The microstructure of MnFeCoNi HEAs after DCD primarily consists of a matrix phase and nano-scale precipitated phase ( σ phase).
The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the matrix Fig. 3 a confirms an FCC crystal structure.
The results show that the phase composition of the HEA remains unchanged after annealing, confirming that DCD followed by annealing at 600 ◦ C does not induce phase transformation.
